item.title: Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A…
item.description:
Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A boil, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A dart, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Bondage, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Mud, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. The womb, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures.
How, bhikkhus, is fear a designation for sensual pleasures? Because those who are infatuated by sensual desire, bound by sensual lust, are not freed from fear in the present life, not freed from fear in the future; therefore, fear is a designation for sensual pleasures.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.56

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion;…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion; one gives out of fear; one gives thinking: 'Earlier our ancestors gave, they did this before. It is not proper for me to let this ancient tradition be neglected'; one gives thinking: 'Having given this gift, after death, with the breakup of the body, I will be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world'; one gives thinking: 'When I give this gift, my mind becomes serene, and joy and happiness arise'; one gives for the adornment of the mind, for the equipment of the mind. Bhikkhus, these are the eight bases for giving.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.33

item.title: Elder Nun Bhaddā: I am the heir of the Buddha, Kassapa, well-concentrated. I know my past lives, See heavenly and hellish realms. The seer who…
item.description:
Elder Nun Bhaddā:

I am the heir of the Buddha,
Kassapa, well-concentrated.
I know my past lives,
See heavenly and hellish realms.

The seer who has destroyed birth,
Perfect in direct knowledge,
Along with these three knowledges,
Is a brahmin with three knowledges.

So too, you, Bhaddā Kapilānī,
You are one with three knowledges,
You have destroyed death,
Bearing your final body,
Having conquered Māra's army.

Seeing the danger in the world,
We both went forth.
We are tamed, our taints destroyed,
We are cooled, at peace, liberated.

From: Therīgāthā 4.1

item.title: - Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is harming me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will harm me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed someone I love, someone I like...' 'He is harming someone I love, someone I like...' 'He will harm someone I love, someone I like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has benefited someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is benefiting someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will benefit someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Getting angry without reason. Bhikkhus, these are the ten grounds for resentment.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.79

item.title: Bhikkhus, the life span of humans in this world is short, and one must go to the future. Do good deeds, live the holy life.…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, the life span of humans in this world is short, and one must go to the future. Do good deeds, live the holy life. There is nothing that is born that does not die. Bhikkhus, one who lives long lives only a hundred years, or a little more or less." Then Māra approached the Blessed One and spoke this verse to him:

'Day and night do not pass,
Life span does not end,
The life of humans turns around
Like a chariot wheel around its axle.'

( Blessed One ):
'Day and night do pass,
Life span does end,
The lives of people dry up
Like small streams on a mountain.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.10

item.title: - It has been a long time, householder, that you have made this opportunity, namely coming here! - Venerable Sir, for a long time I…
item.description:
- It has been a long time, householder, that you have made this opportunity, namely coming here!
- Venerable Sir, for a long time I have wanted to see the Blessed One, but I have been busy with these many duties, so I could not come to see the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

One skilled in the Dhamma,
Who has heard much Dhamma,
Does not regard anything
As one's own happiness.

Behold the affliction
Of those who have possessions,
Which causes one person
To be bound to another.

From: Udāna 2.5

item.title: - Bhikkhus, it is according to their element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful. The shameful…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, it is according to their element that beings associate and come together. The faithful associate and come together with the faithful. The shameful associate and come together with the shameful. The fearful associate and come together with the fearful. Those of great learning associate and come together with those of great learning. The energetic associate and come together with the energetic. The mindful associate and come together with the mindful. The wise associate and come together with the wise.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 14.17

item.title: - Venerable sir, just as a person who has been satisfied with the highest sweetness no longer craves other inferior sweets. So too, venerable sir,…
item.description:
- Venerable sir, just as a person who has been satisfied with the highest sweetness no longer craves other inferior sweets. So too, venerable sir, having heard the Dhamma of Venerable Gotama, one no longer craves the theories of others, of inferior ascetics and brahmins. Just as, venerable sir, a person who is faint with hunger and fatigue finds a honey cake. With every morsel he tastes, with every morsel he experiences pure sweetness. So too, venerable sir, having heard the Dhamma of Venerable Gotama, he gains joy and serene confidence. Just as, venerable sir, a person finds a sandalwood branch, whether yellow sandalwood or red sandalwood. Wherever he smells it — from the root, the middle, or the tip — he experiences a pure, sublime fragrance. So too, venerable sir, having heard the Dhamma of Venerable Gotama, he experiences delight, experiences joy. Just as, venerable sir, a person who is sick, suffering, gravely ill, and then a physician immediately cures his illness. So too, venerable sir, having heard the Dhamma of Venerable Gotama, then sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are destroyed. Just as, venerable sir, a lotus pond with clear water, sweet water, cool water, limpid water, with well-arranged, beautiful banks. Then a person comes, afflicted by heat, oppressed by heat, tired, thirsty, craving water. After plunging into that lotus pond, after bathing and drinking, all his suffering, tiredness, and fever are appeased. So too, venerable sir, having heard the Dhamma of Venerable Gotama, then all suffering, tiredness, and fever are stilled.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.194

item.title: Beautiful are the trees in the forest With blossoming flowers at their tips, In the hot summer months, The first days of summer. So is…
item.description:
Beautiful are the trees in the forest
With blossoming flowers at their tips,
In the hot summer months,
The first days of summer.
So is the supreme Dhamma taught,
Leading to Nibbāna, the supreme bliss.
Thus, in the Buddha there is this excellent jewel.
By this truth, may there be happiness.

The Supreme One knows the Supreme,
Gives the Supreme,
Brings the Supreme —
The unsurpassed Teacher speaks the supreme Dhamma.
Thus, in the Buddha there is this excellent jewel.
By this truth, may there be happiness.

Old kamma is destroyed,
New kamma is not produced,
The mind is free from longing for future existence.
The seeds are destroyed,
Desire does not grow.
The wise realize Nibbāna,
Like this lamp going out.
Thus, in the Saṅgha there is this excellent jewel.
By this truth, may there be happiness.

From: Khuddakapāṭha 6

item.title: Then Māra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he spoke this verse to the Blessed One: Why are you still sleeping, Why are you still…
item.description:
Then Māra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he spoke this verse to the Blessed One:
Why are you still sleeping,
Why are you still sleeping,
Why do you sleep like this,
Like a dead man curled up?
Thinking the house is empty,
Thus you sleep,
Why do you sleep like this
When the sun has risen?

( Blessed One ):
When there is no craving,
With its net and poison,
One thus freed
Is not led anywhere.
Māra! The Enlightened One,
All attachments destroyed,
If he sleeps,
What can you do?

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.7
